evidence: Concrete interruption: a create-seat mutation is durably admitted, then the sole worker writes the shared checkout and crashes before Git commit; alternatively it commits and crashes before recording completion. Admission and completion are expressly distinct (DESIGN-NOTES.md:150), while graph state is Git-backed (DESIGN-NOTES.md:28) and reconciliation must follow latest committed intent (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:14-16; DESIGN-NOTES.md:179). On restart the first case leaves checkout files ahead of committed intent, and the second leaves an admitted request without a completion record. The design specifies neither how startup restores/ignores uncommitted checkout changes nor how a committed mutation is correlated to its journal request before replay or status reporting; mutation/journal contracts are explicitly next design work (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:53; DESIGN-NOTES.md:159 labels inspectable operation status a proposal). If the first checkout is treated as intent, reconciliation may drive an uncommitted seat; if the second request is replayed or left pending without commit correlation, the operation can be applied twice or reported unfinished. Either path conflicts with latest-committed-intent reconciliation and the stated visible, repairable partial-operation promise (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:92-98,139). This is a material acknowledged design gap, not evidence that an implementation already loses data or that the draft claims implementation readiness (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:58).
